Topics · Hard times

I made a choice I regret. Can I begin again?

Regret meets mercy in the Quran, turning is followed by mending, then guidance to a next step. Today is new.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Part 1 of 3

﴿قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ ۖ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. May Allāh forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.

Quran · Yusuf 12:92

Everything has two handles, one by which it may be borne, the other by which it may not. If your brother sin against you lay not hold of it by the handle of injustice, for by that it may not be borne: but rather by this, that he is your brother, the comrade of your youth; and thus you will lay hold on it so that it may be borne.

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 174

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

The Quran has a rare scene: a man who was gravely wronged stands before those who wronged him, with the matter in his hands, and tells them there is no blame on them today, and asks God to forgive them. He does not deny what happened. He sets blame aside. So someone who regrets can find in the book a scene where regret is met with mercy.

A question for you

What weighs on you most?

If you sayThat I hurt someone.
ThenThat regret deserves respect. The next step names repair as part of returning.
If you sayThat I lost a chance that will not return.
ThenThe loss is real. And the verse still speaks of a today with no blame in it.
If you sayI do not know how to forgive myself.
ThenThat question deserves its own page, and it is waiting for you.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا فَقُلْ سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ ۖ أَنَّهُۥ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوٓءًۢا بِجَهَـٰلَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُۥ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when those come to you who believe in Our verses, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:54

Translation

Tell them, ‘“As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn, turn from your evil ways! For why will you die, house of Israel?”’

Original · Hebrew

אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי־אָ֣נִי ׀ נְאֻ֣ם ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם־בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

Ezekiel · 33:11

World English Bible

The verse says your Lord has written mercy upon Himself, and that whoever does wrong out of ignorance, then turns back and mends, will find God forgiving and merciful. The mercy is written by God on Himself, a commitment and not a mood. And the turning is followed by a word, mend: repair what can be repaired. So a fresh start is not only a feeling but a step.

A question for you

Which is closest to what you need?

If you sayA repair that is possible.
ThenBegin there, even if small. The verse puts it on the road.
If you sayNo repair is possible: the person is gone.
ThenThere is a prayer wide enough for this, on another page.
If you sayI fear the mercy is for someone else.
ThenThe mercy is written on God's own self. And it names whom it covers: one who turned back and mended.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِنِّى لَغَفَّارٌ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.

Quran · Ta-Ha 20:82

Translation

All the paths of Yahweh are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.

Original · Hebrew

כָּל־אָרְח֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֑ת לְנֹצְרֵ֥י בְ֝רִית֗וֹ וְעֵדֹתָֽיו׃

the Psalms · 25:10

World English Bible

God says: I am constantly forgiving to one who turns back, believes, does good, and then is guided. Notice the last word: then is guided. The road continues after the turning. So beginning again is not wiping the past but having a road open before you. You do not live behind the mistake. You live after it, and forward.

A question for you

What do you take from this page?

If you sayA new day.
ThenThat is where the page began, and where it ends.
If you sayA specific step.
ThenWrite it down. A written step is closer to happening.
If you saySome days I do not want to go on.
ThenThis app cannot hear you or reach anyone for you, so please do not carry this alone. Talk today to someone you trust, a doctor, or a helpline where you live, and if you are in danger now, reach for the nearest person who can help.

The same in the other books

Translation

“But if the wicked turns from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my statutes, and does that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live. He shall not die. None of his transgressions that he has committed will be remembered against him. In his righteousness that he has done, he shall live.

Original · Hebrew

וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ מִכָּל־חַטֹּאתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְשָׁמַר֙ אֶת־כָּל־חֻקּוֹתַ֔י וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃ כָּל־פְּשָׁעָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לֹ֥א יִזָּכְר֖וּ ל֑וֹ בְּצִדְקָת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

Ezekiel · 18:21-22

World English Bible

Translation

Again, when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed, and does that which is lawful and right, he will save his soul alive. Because he considers, and turns away from all his transgressions that he has committed, he shall surely live. He shall not die.

Original · Hebrew

וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה ה֖וּא אֶת־נַפְשׁ֥וֹ יְחַיֶּֽה׃ וַיִּרְאֶ֣ה וַיָּ֔שָׁב מִכָּל־פְּשָׁעָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה חָי֥וֹ יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

Ezekiel · 18:27-28

World English Bible
